title: Quarter Handoff: Ops Blueprint & Exec Prep (v0.1)
content:
Purpose:

Quick working draft to align the company leadership and ops teams on the Q1 handoff: proposed company-level OKRs, the short exec-update script for the next all-hands, and an operational checklist for a smooth cross-team transition. This is intentionally terse — a living doc for iteration before we lock the all-hands slide set and exec talking points.

Context and constraints:
- We finished a heavy bandwidth quarter (Q4 2024) with multiple Dedicated customer migrations and a Private pilot. Velocity trade-offs impacted a few product launches.
- Exec asks: tighter signal on cost/unit improvements, a short narrative about incident posture improvements, and a crisp set of priorities so teams can commit to measurable outcomes.
- Timeline: need final OKR set and all-hands script by 2025-02-10 to have design + comms ready by 2025-02-14.

Top-level narrative (one-liner to use in emails/slide headlines):
"From stabilization to acceleration: finish the migration backlog, lock cost-per-token playbooks, and scale SRE runbooks so customers get predictable latency at declining unit cost."

Draft company-level OKRs (Q1 2025) — working, measurable, owner-tagged:
Objective A: Reduce inference unit cost while maintaining quality and latency commitments.
- KR A1: Reduce median per-token infra cost by 22% vs. baseline (baseline: $0.0078/token) — owner: Finance + Runtime (David Park).
- KR A2: Ship two quantized model variants (8-bit + mixed-int8) for top-3 hosted models with CI quality gate (<1.5% perplexity delta) — owner: Applied ML (Elena Morales).
- KR A3: Deliver prefix/KV cache autopilot for at least 3 major customers with observed token-savings >= 18% — owner: Serving Runtime (Tomás Hernández).

Objective B: Improve platform reliability and observable signal for latency SLOs.
- KR B1: Reduce P95 inference latency for small-batch chat flows by 12% in hosted (region US-west) — owner: SRE (Priya Kapoor).
- KR B2: Achieve on-call MTTR median <= 18 minutes for production inference incidents — owner: SRE Lead (Priya Kapoor).
- KR B3: Increase traces + token-level cost attribution coverage to 85% of production traffic — owner: Console & Observability (Aisha Raman).

Objective C: Accelerate customer-facing launches and enterprise readiness.
- KR C1: Complete Private beta package and one on-prem pilot, with pass/fail checklist completed — owner: Private Deployments (Ravi Shah).
- KR C2: Convert 3 mid-market trials to Dedicated pilots with contract terms > $50k ARR each — owner: Customer Success (Janelle Park).
- KR C3: Publish two public case studies + one benchmark (latency vs. cost) used in sales enablement — owner: GTM (Marketing lead).

Notes on measurability + acceptance gates:
- All KRs require a short metric definition doc (owner + metric source + query) before we mark as committed. Add to linked_artifacts in the final doc.
- Quality gates must be automated (unit + regression evals) for model changes; manual signoff allowed for experimental rollouts but must be flagged in rollout policy.

Exec update: 3-minute script (for CEO / CTO / COO bullets)
- 0:00 — 0:20 (CEO): Quick framing — "We moved from chaos to chassis: stabilized infra, now we optimize economics and developer velocity."
- 0:20 — 1:20 (CTO): What we shipped — highlight Dedicated migrations, Private pilot readiness, and runtime optimizations (KV cache autopilot) + the impact (cost and latency numbers).
- 1:20 — 2:20 (COO): Customer momentum — three Dedicated trials converted, renewed enterprise contract patterns, and how product + success will drive Q1 revenue.
- 2:20 — 3:00 (Product lead): Ask to company — focus capacity on KR-driven work, freeze non-critical mid-quarter scope, and participate in launch week incident drills.

All-Hands run of show (30 minutes total):
- 0:00–02:00: Welcome + headline (CEO)
- 02:00–06:00: State of product and infra (CTO) — show two slide panels: cost trend, latency trend, incidents trend.
- 06:00–12:00: Customer successes + pilots (GTM + CSM)
- 12:00–18:00: OKR walkthrough (Product + Ops) — present the 3 objectives and call out team-level asks.
- 18:00–24:00: Operational commitments (SRE) — new on-call playbook highlights and MTTR target ask.
- 24:00–30:00: Live Q&A (moderated)

Logistics and assets to produce this week:
- All-hands slide skeleton (Design): 2 slides per speaker, actionable KPI slides for infra, product, and GTM — due 2025-02-07 (Design: Zoe).
- One-pager exec briefing (1 page): CEO + CTO talking points + a 1-line ask for the company — due 2025-02-07 (Owner: Maya).
- Slack comm + FAQ doc for employees (Comms): short reasons and what to focus on — due 2025-02-09 (Owner: People Ops).

Risk register (top 6 short risks and mitigations):
1) Risk: Cost reductions require model changes that could harm quality.
   Mitigation: Lock a quality regression harness + staged canary with automatic rollback; no full rollout without pass.
2) Risk: SRE bandwidth stretched by Dedicated migrations causing higher MTTR.
   Mitigation: Post-migration war room + temporary escalation hotfix rotation; pre-book vendor/contractor on-call buffer.
3) Risk: Sales pipeline misses conversion targets due to competing product gaps.
   Mitigation: Prioritize three conversion blockers as tactical tickets with 2-week cycles.
4) Risk: Communications not crisp -> erosion of company focus.
   Mitigation: Exec one-pager + team-level short standups to translate OKRs to weekly work.
5) Risk: Private pilot delays from security/legal review.
   Mitigation: Assign legal liaison and weekly check-in; produce minimal compliance checklist early.
6) Risk: Observability instrumentation gaps delay acceptance of KR B3.
   Mitigation: Scoped instrumentation sprint with outreach to two high-volume customers to validate traces.

Open decisions (items that must be resolved before commit):
- Commit/no-commit threshold for KR A1: is 20% the minimum or do we keep 22%? (deadline: 2025-01-20, decision owner: Finance).
- Which two hosted models are "top-3" for KR A2? Proposed: redwood-llama-v2, openchat-turbo, and llama-3-mini (owner: Applied ML).
- Do we run a 2-week focused blackout on feature launches during the first migration wave? (owner: Product ops).

Next steps and immediate owners (this week):
- Maya: finalize one-pager exec brief v0.2 — due 2025-01-15.
- Aisha: produce telemetry slide data pulls + query snippets for P95/P50/P99 — due 2025-01-17.
- David: financial model update for per-token baseline + sensitivity table — due 2025-01-18.
- Tomás: scope for KV cache autopilot pilot customers + rollout plan — due 2025-01-20.
- Priya: propose on-call MTTR escalation ladder and draft runbook changes — due 2025-01-19.

Measuring success for the handoff (how we'll know we did this well):
- Execs sign off on final OKRs by 2025-02-10.
- All-hands slides + comms published, employee survey shows >= 75% clarity on priorities.
- First 6 weeks: measurable progress on at least 2 KRs (staging signals or small wins).

Appendix — quick metric snapshot (latest week):
- Hosted median per-token infra cost: $0.0078 (baseline used above).
- P95 small-batch chat latency (US-west): 240 ms (target to reduce to ~211 ms).
- Production incidents (last 90d): 7 Sev2/3 incidents, median MTTR 34 min (target: <=18).
- Dedicated migration backlog: 9 customers in pipeline; 3 in final onboarding phase.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally concise and tactical. Please add comments inline where you see conflicting priorities.
- If you’re an exec: focus comments on the headline narrative and the KR measurability notes.
- If you’re an IC or manager: add suggested owners for any KR or metric where you can commit time.

Quick TODOs (inline):
- [ ] Design: slide skeleton assigned to Zoe (due 2025-02-07)
- [ ] Exec brief v0.2 (Maya) (due 2025-01-15)
- [ ] Instrumentation query list (Aisha) (due 2025-01-17)

History/version notes: v0.1 created 2025-01-12 by Maya Chen — initial pass combining ops + product asks.
